title: Sharp Bounds for Net Benefit Shares from Fused Trial and Self-Selection Data
banked_reason: The note proves a matched local asymptotic minimax reduction only for a highly calibrated eighteen-cell experiment, while the resulting Gaussian value V(H0) remains an unsolved infimum-supremum.
gap_reasons: The note proves a matched local asymptotic minimax reduction only for a highly calibrated eighteen-cell experiment, while the resulting Gaussian value V(H0) remains an unsolved infimum-supremum.
At H0=1 the sole instantiated enclosure, 0.2943<V(1)<8.174, is too loose to determine the sampling cost or provide a practically meaningful rule.
The uniform center, three bins, fair assignment, equal independent sample sizes, and fixed local box sharply limit applicability to the prospective fused-data consumer.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery verified sharp transport endpoints, the exact local contrast, compact Gaussian saddle, and a source-attested two-way multinomial–Gaussian comparison; the D0.5 math panel passed. The field-tier attempt stopped because the value remained an implicit Gaussian game with a loose numeric enclosure and no usable evaluated rule. The finite-support saddle/value certificate remains an open problem; D0.5 decision-panel positioning findings were left unrepaired because they cannot lift the calibrated tier.
tldr: A fair trial identifies the marginal outcome-bin laws, while a self-selection sample identifies how those margins vary with latent treatment preference. For the net share with a decisive positive rather than negative individual gain, the fused compatibility fiber yields global sharp endpoints that are sums of three-face transport formulas, and at the uniform eighteen-cell center their endpoint sum becomes an exact nonodd piecewise-linear contrast. The note characterizes the all-rule binary minimax value over a fixed bounded local box, proves an attained Gaussian saddle with a least-favorable measure, gives outward-convergent finite certificates, and transfers the value and a deterministic ordered-record rule at \(O(n^{-1/2})\). The target is expected excess realized robust loss relative to a deterministic robust oracle, not an integrated local criterion or a randomized population allocation.
gap: Existing fused-data work characterizes the compatibility fiber and generic sharp bounds, while existing local decision work studies stochastic population actions, integrated local risk, shrinking identified sets, or linear and centrosymmetric Gaussian games. None of the verified sources gives the exact compact minimax sampling value for the fused signed-gain binary decision under expected realized robust loss.
fill: The project derives closed-form sharp endpoints, an exact active-face contrast, a two-way all-rule experiment transfer, a positive compact Gaussian value, outward-convergent finite programs, and a legal deterministic binary sample rule that attains the value.
